title: Cambodia Becomes Ninth Country To Accept UPI Payments After NPCI International-ACLEDA Bank Tie-Up
text:
Economy
Swarajya Staff
Jun 04, 2026 | Updated 09:05 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!
Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.
Cambodia has become the ninth country to accept UPI payments, after NPCI International Payments Limited and ACLEDA Bank Plc. launched UPI acceptance through KHQR, Cambodia’s national QR code, enabling 4.5 million merchant outlets across the Southeast Asian nation to accept payments from Indian travellers.
The partnership went live following a ceremony in Phnom Penh attended by Chea Serey, Governor of the National Bank of Cambodia, alongside Reserve Bank of India representatives.
Indian tourists can now make seamless QR-based payments at restaurants, retail stores and tourist attractions using their familiar UPI-enabled applications, eliminating the need for currency exchange or carrying large amounts of cash.
Cambodia joins Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar and Sri Lanka in accepting UPI payments.
The first phase focuses on Indian visitors making payments in Cambodia, while a planned second phase will enable Cambodian citizens to use their domestic banking applications at UPI-enabled merchant locations throughout India, creating a fully bi-directional payment corridor.
The initiative aims to enhance real-time payment connectivity between the two countries while strengthening tourism and commercial ties.
Cambodian merchants gain access to India's tech-savvy consumer demographic, whilst benefiting from improved cash management and reduced reliance on physical currency.
UPI processed 23.20 billion transactions worth nearly Rs 30 lakh crore in May alone, demonstrating the platform's massive domestic reach.
